To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the spacer fragment length polymorphisms between 16S rRNA and 23S RNA genes of Salmonella enteric are useful for typing at serotype and, to a lesser extent, at subspecies levels.

the length of the internal transscribed spacer between the 16S and the 23S rDNA gene was found to vary among Salmonella strains and the ITS‐PCR technique was used to discriminate between Salmonella serotypes.
the spacer fragment length polymorphisms of 16S to 238 rRNA genes in Salmonella enterica are useful in subspecies and serotypes typing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of the ITS as a genetic marker in Salmonella enterica.

the application of PCR and automated sequencing to the characterization of the ITSs of Salm. entericaribotypes and the potential of ITS‐based PCR for the rapid identification and characterization of Salmonella.
the development of a new molecular typing method for Salm. enterida.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ITS length polymorphisms are not a suitable marker for typing Salm. enterida at subspecies and/or serotype levels.
this method is not yet suitable as a typing tool at serotype or subspecies level, although it is promising at subspecies level.
the ITS‐PCR‐based method is not suitable for typing of Salmonella enteric at serotype and/or subspecies level.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the ITS length polymorphism can be used for typing of Salm. enterida at subspecies level, but not at serotype level, and it is not suitable for differentiating subspecies. 16S to 238 rRNA spacer fragment polymorphism of
the ITS‐PCR method can be used for typing Salm. enterida at the subspecies level and that some serotypes are sufficiently differentiated by this method.

the 16S to 235 rRNA spacer fragment pattern is a useful tool for typing Salmonella enterica strains at the serotype and subspp. level, but it is not a reliable marker for the identification of Salmonella enteritidis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ITS region is highly variable within Salm. cholerasuis and can be used to differentiate between serotypes and subspecies.
the ITS spacer length polymorphism can be used for typing Salmonella enterica subspecies and serotypes.
the ITS is a useful genetic marker for Salmonella typing at the serotype level.
